title: S10 render — first visual drafts, with the refusal/fallback trail

attempts.description: Ordered. named_variant first, attribute_variant on refusal. Refusals are logged verbatim, never silently dropped.

status.description: The three failure states are editorially load-bearing and must never be collapsed into one another — the charter and the UI both key off the distinction. 'refused' = a renderer was reached and DECLINED ON POLICY GROUNDS; that is an editorial signal about the concept and the next variant must be tried. 'error' = a renderer was reached and failed transiently (timeout, crash, malformed output); retrying the same variant is legitimate. 'unavailable' = no renderer was reachable at all — nothing was ever asked of a model, so this says nothing whatsoever about the concept and must not be read as a refusal.

model.description: Free text naming whatever tool this attempt actually used — a local renderer, a command-line image tool, a hosted generator the agent could reach without a key. It is NOT an API model id and nothing keys off its value; it exists so the editor can tell what produced (or failed to produce) the draft.

refusal_text.description: Verbatim, for status 'refused' only. Never paraphrase a policy decline — the exact wording is what tells the editor whether the concept itself is the problem.

error.description: For 'error', the transient failure. For 'unavailable', which renderer was looked for and how it was found to be absent.

asset_path.description: Relative to the run directory, e.g. 10_drafts/st_x_cp_y_1.png

outcome.description: 'all_variants_refused' means every variant was put to a renderer and declined on policy grounds — an editorial finding about the concept, which the gate and the editor must see. 'no_renderer_available' means the agent could not reach any renderer at all, so the concept was never judged; it is an honest 'we could not draw this here', not a verdict on the idea. Recording the second as the first would silently indict a concept nothing ever looked at.
